title: Documentation and Changelog
hints: User-facing behavior changes may need documentation or changelog entries.
This is the core-repository side. A project extension uses its own manual, semantic version and release notes; see extension-documentation.
A changelog file is needed for a Breaking change, a Deprecation, a Feature, or an Important message. A casual bug fix needs none — its commit message carries the information.

Which of the four is decided by what the patch does: Breaking where core functionality third-party code may call was moved, removed or had its signature changed — adding a parameter changes one, an optional parameter included — Deprecation where it is marked for a planned removal, Feature where functionality is added, Important for anything else that may require manual action. Important is the last resort and the only type an LTS release carries, because those take no feature, deprecation or breaking entries.

The filename is <Type>-<forgeIssueNumber>-<UpperCamelCaseDescription>.rst, in the directory of the minor version the change is released in; a backport goes into the <lts>.x directory of the oldest branch it reaches, in every branch that carries it.

The core ships the skeleton, so it is copied rather than assembled: Build/rstTemplates/rstTemplate<Type>.rst per type, with {ISSUE}, {TITLE} and {TIMESTAMP} to substitute. ./Build/Scripts/runTests.sh -s watchRst core interactive writes one from it, asks for the type, the issue and the title, and renders it live while it is edited. It writes into the directory of the release that branch develops, so a backport's file is moved afterwards.

The file opens with an include of /Includes.rst.txt, then an anchor of the form <type>-<issue>-<unix timestamp>, then the title "Type: #<issue> - <summary>" fenced by a row of = above and below it, then "See :issue:`<issue>`". The anchor sits directly above the title with only blank lines between them, and it has to be unique across the whole changelog tree, which is what the timestamp is for.

Every type has a Description section; a Feature, a Deprecation and a Breaking have an Impact section; a Deprecation and a Breaking additionally have a Migration section. That is what each type owes, and it is not the shape its entries have: an Important owes no Impact section and plenty of them carry one, and the Affected installations section the Deprecation and Breaking templates ship is in a minority of their entries.

The Important template is the one that disagrees with the tree. It ships Affected installations and Migration, which few Important entries carry, and no Impact, which many do — so copying it as the skeleton above says produces a shape the reviewer will not recognise. Read a neighbouring entry in the directory the file is going into, which is also where the fence and the index tags are read from.

The fence is not measured against the title: validateRstFiles.php asks for two or more = above and below, the shipped templates carry a fixed-width row whatever the title is, and entries whose fence is shorter than their title are merged and rendered. Write it to the title's length, which is what the tree does, and spend no round patching it to the byte.

The include:: and index:: directives take one or two spaces after the leading dots. validateRstFiles.php accepts either, the templates use two, and both spellings stand side by side in one directory — so a file that validates is not rewritten from one to the other.

The .. index:: line is the file's last line, and its tags come from a closed list: Backend, CLI, Database, FAL, FlexForm, Fluid, Frontend, JavaScript, LocalConfiguration, PHP-API, RTE, TCA, TSConfig, TypoScript, YAML and ext:<system extension key>, with TSConfig spelled with that capital C. Howto.rst asks for at least two tags and no more than five. A Deprecation or Breaking file also carries exactly one of NotScanned, PartiallyScanned or FullyScanned.

Nothing registers the file: each directory's Index.rst pulls the types in by a glob toctree, so the filename prefix is the inclusion. A directory whose Index.rst replaced a type's toctree with a sentence takes no file of that type, which is what the LTS directories do with Breaking.
A deprecation entry names the replacement and the migration path; without both it does not do its job. Add an extension scanner matcher when the deprecated API can be found statically.

hints.text: Literals in the prose take role markup — :php:, :yaml:, :typoscript:, :file: — rather than plain double backticks, and the section headings under the title are underlined only, while the title itself is fenced above and below. checkRst reports neither: it reads the include, the title, the See :issue: reference, the anchor and the index line, and the render is what shows the rest. typo3/sysext/core/Documentation/Changelog/Howto.rst is the authority, and Build/Scripts/validateRstFiles.php is the check.

hints: Keep ReST changes focused and validate them before review.

title: Documenting a Project Extension
hints: An extension's manual lives in Documentation/, with Index.rst as its entry point and guides.xml as the renderer configuration. docs.typo3.org renders that tree; the extension does not copy the core's Documentation/Changelog artifact into itself.

A released ViewHelper argument, translation label, configuration key, event payload or PHP API is public to whoever installed the extension. A breaking change is carried by the extension's semantic version and explained in its own release notes and migration documentation.

Keep the manual with the extension so a package release and the documentation for that release are one revision. Repository-wide deployment notes are a different artifact and belong with the project that deploys it.
For a patch to TYPO3 itself, the documentation-changelog hint has the core's release-note filename, structure and checks; those are repository conventions, not a template for an extension.

title: Linking Into the Official Documentation From a Template or From PHP
hints: A link into the official documentation is built from a permalink identifier and never written out as a URL. The branch of the running installation is appended to it, so the reader lands on the documentation of the TYPO3 they are on and a backport carries the link unchanged.

The identifier is the one the link modal of a rendered manual shows: t3coreapi:extension-scanner, t3tsref:cobj-pageview. An identifier that already carries an @ is rejected with exception 1728643940, an InvalidArgumentException.

Whether an identifier resolves, what page and anchor it lands on, and which identifier replaces a docs.typo3.org URL already in the code is typo3_permalink_lookup. A guessed one is an HTTP 404 that nothing in a checkout reports, and the identifier does not follow from the page path: the low-level manual answers typo3-cms-lowlevel:typo3-low-level and not :start.

In a Fluid template that is <be:link.documentation identifier="t3coreapi:extension-scanner">the official docs</be:link.documentation> rather than an a element written by hand. The be prefix is declared per template, and fluid-templates carries the declaration.
The rendered a element forces target="_blank" and rel="noreferrer". Passing either is overwritten with nothing raised, so leave both out; class and every other attribute reaches the tag as given.

An install-tool template may use it because it takes no constructor argument: under the failsafe container ViewHelperResolver builds a ViewHelper through makeInstance(). Only a ViewHelper with required constructor arguments has to be registered in install/Classes/ServiceProvider.php first, which is what the handful listed there are.
The ViewHelper class is marked @internal and not part of TYPO3 Core API. A backend module outside the core may call it and is given no promise that it survives the next major.

hints.text: From PHP the same link is Typo3Information::getDocsLink('t3coreapi:...'), static so that a message can build one before DI is ready. The core writes it into deprecation messages, TypoScript error messages and install-tool environment checks.
From PHP the same link is (new Typo3Information())->getDocsLink('t3coreapi:...'). The method is not static here, so early-bootstrap code that cannot construct the object writes the URL out instead.
Typo3Information has no permalink method here and the ViewHelper builds the URL itself, so PHP that needs such a link writes it out. Only the template side of this subject exists on this branch.
